summary.headline: Ratnamani Q4 FY26 standalone sales fell to INR893 crore from INR1,575 crore; FY27 standalone budget set at INR4,800-5,000 crore assuming quick normalisation.
summary.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 sales were INR893 crore versus INR1,575 crore a year earlier, with the decline driven by lower carbon steel volumes while stainless steel was broadly flat. Consolidated Q4 sales were INR1,085 crore (vs INR1,715 crore) and FY26 consolidated sales were INR4,494 crore (vs INR5,186 crore), though management said group EBITDA margin % and absolute EBITDA and PAT were broadly maintained. Standalone order book was about INR2,160 crore as of 1 May 2026, of which INR697 crore was export and INR531 crore stainless steel. The Board cut the dividend to INR10 per share, citing conservation of resources amid Middle East disruption and muted demand.

vs INR1,715 crore in Q4 FY25
500% of face value; lower than prior year
standalone debt-free for regular bank limits; only minor FD-OD utilisation

segments.name: Standalone carbon steel
segments.commentary: Volumes fell sharply in H2 (about 40% decline per analyst read-out, not disputed) as capacity was shifted from one location to another; Orissa production restarted and Kutch can now make pipes up to 18 m. Mix shifted from water (Jal Jeevan) to oil and gas.

segments.name: Standalone stainless steel
segments.commentary: Volumes grew in FY26 but prices fell, leaving revenue roughly flat; management says realisations are now 5-10% higher YoY. Order book INR531 crore as of 1 May 2026.

segments.name: Ravi Technoforge (RTL)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR105 crore (+28%); FY27 growth guidance trimmed to 10-15% from 15-20% until new capacity (auto parts segment) comes on line in FY28.

segments.name: Ratnamani Finow Spooling Solutions (RFSS)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR72 crore (~+60%); FY26 INR390 crore. Spool order book about INR550 crore, with INR480-500 crore planned for execution in FY27; FY27 growth guided at 20-25%, margin expected to settle at 20-25%. New facility to contribute from H2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Standalone FY27 budget INR4,800-5,000 crore; management said this assumes normalisation within about a month and current raw material prices, with orders largely back-to-back.
Standalone EBITDA margin of 16% plus/minus 1% seen as sustainable, but would be a 'totally different scenario' if the conflict extends beyond 3-5 months.
RTL FY27 growth 10-15%; RFSS FY27 growth 20-25%, with margin 20-25% going forward.
Standalone capex excluding Saudi project routine at INR150-200 crore per year; Saudi cold-finished project is the one major capex.
Middle East greenfield plant: design complete and submitted for approval; trials targeted by March 2027, with possible slippage of up to three months.
capex_capacity: Standalone routine capex INR150-200 crore per year, plus one Saudi capex project (cold-finished).
Stainless steel debottlenecking under way (instrumentation tubes in straight length; coil-form orders being executed); new tube mill planned on the welded side, not separately highlighted.
Carbon steel: 18 m spiral welded pipe capability added; API 5CT range expanded during FY26.
RFSS new manufacturing facility expected to contribute revenue from H2 FY27.
RTL expansion (capacity, automation, precision) processing well; new capacity to enable auto parts segment from FY28.
demand_pricing: Standalone order book about INR2,000 crore through FY26; INR2,160-2,162 crore as of 1 May 2026, of which export INR697 crore, stainless INR531 crore, carbon steel INR1,631 crore.
Inquiries improving across markets: domestic gas transmission, refinery and petrochemical (stainless), renewables, and thermal power heater and condenser tubes.

Middle East oil and gas projects are on paper but not yet converting to orders; shipping constraints and high vessel costs are delaying dispatch. About INR100-150 crore of material was stuck last year because of the conflict.
Stainless steel competition rising from carbon steel players, but new capacity is largely pierced seamless, which Ratnamani does not serve; only one new extruded player expected, timing unknown.
Total spool bidding pipeline about USD400-500 million; no historical win-rate reference. Water-related order exposure INR300-400 crore.
Management noted pierced tube acceptance is growing in power; some end users are restricting to extruded tubes.

qa_highlights.question: Is there structural margin decline in stainless steel given excess capacity, and where would incremental cash be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said stainless volumes rose in FY26 while prices fell; focus stays on high-value extruded products. Only debottlenecking capex is planned, not separately disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Standalone FY27 realisation and volume breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: Stainless realisations up 5-10% YoY; carbon steel volumes were down due to capacity shift. Standalone budget INR4,800-5,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Cash and debt position?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Vimal Katta said about INR800 crore of free cash; standalone debt-free for regular bank limits, with minor FD-OD usage.

qa_highlights.question: Is INR4,800-5,000 crore target inclusive of delayed dispatches?
qa_highlights.answer: Target assumes normalisation soon; the delayed dispatches are considered part of the normalisation case, not added upside. It assumes current pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Is 16-18% margin sustainable and what is the forex impact?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said 16-18% is sustainable in the longer run, with 1% variance possible. FY26 forex gain about INR45 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to Middle East and CGD demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Middle East O&G inquiries not yet converted due to shipping cost and availability. CGD demand is mostly ERW and lags pipe procurement; government push expected to help over time, with timing uncertain.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict duration: management said a conflict extending beyond 3-5 months would make the INR4,800-5,000 crore FY27 budget and 16% plus/minus 1% margin unachievable.
Shipping and freight costs and port access limit export dispatches; order conversion in O&G is still awaited.
Carbon steel volume recovery and mix shift away from water projects.
Stainless steel price pressure from new capacity; pierced seamless adoption could compress power-sector margins in the short term.
Gas cost increase on carbon steel and some stainless heat-treatment furnaces; magnitude not disclosed.
EU carbon border adjustment mechanism and export quota changes, with long-term local capacity risk.
Standalone order book only modestly above last year's level, which management says is supported by capacity returning rather than new wins.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term demand and the subsidiaries, but cautious near term: CEO repeatedly tied FY27 guidance to normalisation within about a month and gave a conditional margin view. Answers on spool margins and the stainless capex outlook were less specific.
key_quotes: So, we still remain confident that the project can be finished within March 2027.
The stainless-steel volume in the last fiscal year actually went up, not down, but the prices were down.
Margins say, 16% plus/minus 1%, definitely, it can be maintained. However, if the conflict that we see today extends, say, beyond 3, 4, 5 months, then it will be a totally different scenario.

growth.why: Standalone FY27 budget of INR4,800-5,000 crore (vs FY26 standalone decline in Q4 of 43% YoY) rests on a ~INR2,160 crore order book, normalisation within about a month and back-to-back orders, with RFSS 20-25% and RTL 10-15% growth guided and new RFSS facility from H2 FY27.
